tagline.text: A triple-tiered waterfall hidden beyond the coconut groves of Samboan

location.label: Location
location.text: Binalayan area, Barangay Bonbon, Samboan, Cebu

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Dry season, December–May (check water level and clarity after rain)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,200 (day trip from Cebu City, depending on how you travel)

children.text: Binalayan Falls is tucked away inside Barangay Bonbon in Samboan, at the southwestern tip of Cebu. The water drops in three streams, which is why it is also called Triple Drop Falls. A walk of
15–20 minutes
through coconut groves brings you there, and you can swim or jump in from the lower ledges.

Binalayan Falls is a waterfall in the Bonbon area of Samboan, a town at the southwestern tip of Cebu Island. Locally it is also called Hidden Falls or Triple Drop Falls. As the name suggests, you cannot see it from the main road; you reach it by following a path through coconut farms and crossing shallow streams. Samboan has so many waterfalls that it is nicknamed the "Waterfall Capital of Cebu," and Binalayan is one of the easiest to reach because the walk is short.

The falls come in two stages. From the entrance you first reach a small waterfall and a green pool with a tire swing, which is the gentlest place to get into the water for the first time. A little farther up is the main fall, about

high, where the water splits into three streams. There is a small cave behind it, and many visitors jump into the pool from low rocks. Some writers say the second fall is the reason for the name "Hidden."
The route is not difficult. From the entrance, where you will find the parking area and ticket office, you walk about
15–20 minutes

on flat ground through a coconut grove and cross a shallow stream several times along the way. Expect wet feet and wear water shoes or sandals with straps. A guide normally goes with you; he also takes photos and tells you how deep the water is and where it is safe to jump.
Binalayan lies about
150km

south of Cebu City, so a day trip is possible but the journey is long. A common plan is to base yourself in Moalboal or near Kawasan Falls and combine it with Samboan's other waterfalls (Aguinid and Dao Falls), or to come up from Oslob. This guide compares several accounts written between 2017 and 2026. Fees and closing days have changed over the years, so always confirm them locally.

blocks.title: The main fall in three streams

children.text: The main fall drops down a rock face about
high, splitting into three streams. That is where the name Triple Drop comes from. The volume of water and its color vary with the season and recent rain, so check local conditions before you go.

blocks.title: The first pool with a tire swing

children.text: The smallest fall, which you meet first near the entrance, has a tire swing hung above a green pool and a rest area with benches. If you are not a confident swimmer or you are traveling with children, get used to the water here first. The water is shallow and calm, so this is the safest place to enjoy.
The path from the entrance to the falls runs flat through coconut farms and takes about
15–20 minutes
. You may see coconuts being harvested along the way, and your guide may cut one down for you if you ask. There are several stream crossings, so water shoes are a must.

blocks.title: The cave behind the fall and low jumping spots

children.text: Behind the main fall there is a small cave you can climb into, and the jumping spots are said to be 3–5 m high. However, the pool is only about
2m
deep at its deepest and can be shallower after rain. Always jump feet first, and only from the low spots where your guide has checked the depth.

The small fall on the second tier holds a turquoise pool and is considered a photo highlight. The stone steps up to it are slippery, but bamboo handrails have been installed. Visitors say you can leave belongings near the bamboo railing, but it is safer not to bring valuables.

blocks.title: One stop on Samboan's waterfall circuit

children.text: Besides Aguinid and Dao Falls, Samboan is said to have several more waterfalls, including Candayvic, Calasa, Balay'g Sawa and Tabon Falls. Binalayan is close to Aguinid, so it is easy to link the two by motorbike taxi, and it makes a good middle stop on a waterfall tour of two or three falls in a day.

The entrance has a parking area, a ticket office and a starting point, and the entrance fee includes the guide and an environmental fee. There are not many facilities compared with big tourist sites, but that also means it can be quiet on weekdays. No information on restrooms, restaurants or shops could be confirmed, so prepare in the town beforehand.

items.title: Day trip from Cebu City
items.subtitle: By bus to Samboan, then two waterfalls

children.text: Take a bus bound for Bato from the Cebu South Bus Terminal in Cebu City. Some travelers report that getting to Samboan takes about
4–5 hours
, so leave early.
Get off at the Bonbon village stop. Get off at Bonbon rather than in Samboan town proper, because the entrance is closer. From the stop to the entrance, take a tricycle or motorbike taxi.
Pay the entrance fee at the ticket office and set off with your guide. Walk
15–20 minutes
across the flat coconut grove, crossing the stream.
After getting used to the water at the first pool and tire swing, hold the bamboo railing and climb to the second tier.
Swim and take photos at the main fall. Jump only from the low spot your guide points out.
Have lunch in Samboan town, and if you have time left, continue to Aguinid Falls by motorbike taxi.
I could not confirm the time of the last bus back to Cebu City. It is safest to return to the road early in the afternoon and ask locally.
Set out from Moalboal by motorbike or rental car. Binalayan is about
55km
away, roughly
1 hour 20 minutes
by car.
Visit Aguinid Falls first. It has several tiers, so allow plenty of time.
Move on to Binalayan, walk the trail and swim at the main fall.
Choose Dao Falls or another waterfall depending on the time, and return to Moalboal before dark.
On days when you visit several waterfalls, riding a motorbike for a long time in wet clothes gets cold. Bring a change of clothes and a waterproof bag.
Direct flights run frequently from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), taking about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Check the airline's official website for the latest schedules and fares.
From the airport, a taxi or ride-hailing car is the easiest way to reach the Cebu South Bus Terminal in Cebu City.
Samboan is about
150km
from Cebu City. A day trip is possible, but if you want to visit two or more places, it is better to stay a night in Moalboal or Oslob.
Take a bus bound for Bato (via Barili) from the Cebu South Bus Terminal in Cebu City and get off at Bonbon village.
Travel time is given as 3.5–4 hours in a 2017 article and 4–5 hours in articles from 2022 onward, a big difference. It varies with traffic, so allow plenty of time.
The fare was reported as about ₱170–210 in 2017 and about ₱300 in July 2025, so it has changed over the years. Ask the conductor again when you board.
From Bonbon to the entrance, take a tricycle or motorbike taxi.
It is about
23km
from Oslob, roughly
30 minutes
by car. From Moalboal it is about
55km
, roughly
1 hour 20 minutes
by car.
Search for "Binalayan Hidden Falls" in Google Maps or Waze for directions. The entrance is a few meters off the main road, and there is a parking area.
One traveler reports that a motorbike rental in Cebu costs about ₱400 per day.
Motorbike taxis (habal-habal) run from Samboan town to Binalayan. A 2017 article gave ₱20 per person one way, and ₱10 from Binalayan to Aguinid, but fares now appear to be higher.
Some sources say you can also reach Samboan by taking a bus bound for Bato from across the road at Kawasan Falls. Some tricycle drivers at Kawasan offer a waterfall-hopping tour.

Cebu's dry season generally runs from December to May. At this time the water is clear and the trail streams are shallow, which makes it a good time to visit waterfalls. January to April in particular has stable weather for swimming.

In the rainy season from June to November, the falls look more powerful, but the pools become muddy and the stream crossings can be difficult. One guide notes that the pool can actually be shallower after heavy rain, so avoid jumping. When a typhoon approaches the entrance may close or be dangerous, so check local news before you leave.

There are small guesthouses in Samboan, and traveler reports mention Fantasy Lodge and MDF Beach Resort. If you plan to visit several waterfalls, basing yourself in Moalboal or near Kawasan gives you more choices. Moalboal has everything from hostels to resorts.

No restrooms or restaurants near the entrance could be confirmed, so bring water and snacks. Eat at a local restaurant in Samboan town or in Oslob or Moalboal. At the falls, your guide may cut down a coconut for you, so give it a try.
Wear water shoes or sandals with straps. You will cross streams and climb slippery rocks.
Put your phone and wallet in a waterproof bag, or leave them at your accommodation.
Always jump feet first, and only from a spot where your guide has checked the depth.
Ask locally about the entrance fee and closing day in advance. One article says it is closed on Tuesdays.
If you ask the motorbike taxi driver to wait for you, getting back is easier.
Combining Aguinid Falls and Dao Falls makes a rewarding one-day route.
Carry plenty of small change. Entrance fees and tips are normally paid in cash.
Pack a change of clothes and a towel in a plastic bag.
Even at its deepest, the jumping pool is only about 2 m deep and becomes shallower after rain. Do not dive headfirst and follow your guide's instructions.
The stone steps with bamboo handrails are wet and very slippery. Go up and down slowly.
When it rains heavily, the stream level can rise quickly and become dangerous, so do not go on that day.
No restrooms, restaurants or shops could be confirmed. Prepare what you need beforehand.
Entrance fee and closing-day information differs between articles, so confirm the latest details locally.
